## The Census API challenge

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Where people get stuck**

- The **key**: request it, then keep it out of your code
- **Geography**: state → county → tract → block group
- **Variable names**: `B19013_001E` means something, but you have to look it up
- **Limits**: pull once, cache it, don't loop the API
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.card}
[What makes it done]{.card-title}

A table you can **join to our stores**, with the variables you chose and a sentence on **why those** variables matter to your client.
:::
:::
:::

The `census.*` tables are already in Databricks. **The API work is about learning the pull**, not about getting data we lack.

## The challenges are not the project

Each challenge builds **one piece** of what your team will deliver:

::: {.flow}
::: {.box}
Wrangling

[Polars, charts]{.muted}
:::

[→]{.arrow}

::: {.box}
Census

[outside data]{.muted}
:::

[→]{.arrow}

::: {.box .hl}
Unit of analysis

[one row = ?]{.muted}
:::

[→]{.arrow}

::: {.box}
Features

[the model's inputs]{.muted}
:::

[→]{.arrow}

::: {.box}
App

[someone uses it]{.muted}
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
**The project is the thread through all of them.** Every challenge should move your team's product forward, not sit in a folder by itself.
:::

## What your team owes

- A **unit of analysis** everyone on the team can say out loud
- A **target** the data supports: a probability or a count
- **Features** built at that grain, documented so a teammate can rebuild them
- An **analysis** that answers the business question, not just the model question
- An **app** a non-technical person can use

[Start writing these down now. The grade request letter at the end is much easier when the work is on the record.]{.orange}

## The analysis decks

Three reference decks for the analysis half of the project. **Read them when you need them.**

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
[Baskets of Goods]{.card-title}

Association rules: what sells with what, support, confidence and lift.

[Open →](topics/association_rules.html)
:::
::: {.card}
[Labeled Baskets]{.card-title}

Picking a Y, building the modeling table, and avoiding leakage.

[Open →](topics/basket_models.html)
:::
::: {.card}
[Customer Segmentation]{.card-title}

Clustering, UMAP and HDBSCAN, and how to defend a segment.

[Open →](topics/customer_segmentation.html)
:::
:::

They use **our C-Store data** for their examples, so the numbers should look familiar.

## Thursday: your first take-home challenge

::: {.columns}

- Announced **at least 24 hours** ahead, with the topic
- You may talk with your group, but **you don't share code**

Be able to run a PySpark notebook on Databricks **before Thursday**. Don't spend the challenge fighting your setup.
